findings: Original symptom (process.start -> E_PROCESS_INTERNAL 'Access denied (os error 5)') reproduces only while <workspace>/.ae/process-lifecycle is absent; the executor's first write inside the op is fs::create_dir_all of that path.
With the lifecycle root present, process.start runs normally (cmd.exe /D /C echo probe-ok -> exit 0, stdout probe-ok) on current origin/main without any code change.

The previously gated real-limit suite then fails for two reasons that are wrong assertions, not enforcement gaps: cmd.exe /C needs a helper process so a maxProcesses:1 Job refuses the root; and PowerShell continues past a non-terminating OutOfMemoryException so it still prints alloc-ok.

boundaries: The pre-create is a diagnosability fix, not a sandbox bypass: a host that denies the record write still fails, now with E_PROCESS_PERSIST instead of E_PROCESS_INTERNAL.
No kernel QueryInformationJobObject readback exists; enforcement evidence is behavioural.
The opt-in suite stays opt-in because the bundled binary may be absent.
No product lock/default/release change; agent-driven only.
